title: Linear Equations and Graphs
summary: Equations as balances, solving step by step, turning stories into equations, plotting coordinates, straight-line graphs y = mx + c, and reading the stories that graphs tell.

ib.statementOfInquiry: Equations and graphs model relationships between quantities, helping us find unknowns and make predictions about real situations.

factual: How do we solve a linear equation?
How do we plot points on a coordinate grid?
What do m and c mean in y = mx + c?
conceptual: Why must we do the same thing to both sides of an equation?
How can a graph show a relationship that a table cannot?
debatable: Can every real-life problem be written as an equation?
